papers.title: Implant-supported full-arch rehabilitation with immediate loading using two different digital impression techniques: a case report with 2-year follow-up.
papers.abstract: Immediate full-arch loading is a highly complex and technique-sensitive procedure. Digital impression techniques aim to replace conventional analog systems to carry out dental treatments in a more predictive, safer, and less time-consuming way. This case report describes a patient with a guarded periodontal prognosis, who was rehabilitated with implant-supported fixed prostheses after full-mouth extractions. Immediate full-arch loading was performed by means of two digital impression systems: photogrammetric technology with PIC dental in the maxillary arch, and MedicalFit in the mandible. Immediate provisional prostheses in acrylic resin (polymethyl methacrylate) were milled and placed within 12 hours after implant placement surgeries. Both provisional structures fitted properly providing adequate esthetics and function. After the implant osseointegration period, final digital impressions were registered, and definitive zirconia full-arch implant-supported prostheses were delivered. The 24-month follow-up did not show biologic or mechanical complications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 此论文为临床病例报告，未涉及增材制造、多孔结构、力学测试或应力屏蔽，与用户研究方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical case report with no additive manufacturing, no porous structure analysis, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), and no stress shielding evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 报告即刻负重全口种植修复的数字化印模技术应用。
summary_zh.method: 使用两种数字化印模系统进行全口种植修复。
summary_zh.result: 24个月随访无生物学或机械并发症。

summary_en.motivation: To demonstrate the feasibility of digital impression techniques for immediate loading full-arch implant rehabilitation.
summary_en.method: Two digital impression systems (photogrammetry and MedicalFit) were used for maxillary and mandibular arches, with immediate provisional acrylic prostheses milled within 12 hours.
summary_en.result: No biologic or mechanical complications were observed at 24-month follow-up.
